I always have a first instinct to keep it to myself, with the justification of, "You shouldn't feel like this", "You don't want to present yourself as somebody who is weak in that way", "You are just going to cause emotional turmoil if you bring this up". But I have found that actually, what's problematic is the attachment to a specific outcome. We "keep it to ourselves" because we want "not to cause a problem". We "approach someone in an upset fashion" because we want "them to address our feelings as a means of calming us down". We "display our pain and hurt" because we want "someone to see our complaint as valid", et cetera.

If you completely release the attachment to the outcome, the whole tone of everything changes. With only the disclaimer of, "I just want to share how I'm feeling, I'm not trying to say you should do any one thing in particular", you can just lay out the stimuli from the environment ("you had to stay late at work because you're trying to do your best") and the emotions evoked in your brain and body as a response ("I felt alone and abandoned at a time when I wasn't strong enough to withstand it"), and there's no 'litmus test' of reasonability that you have to pass.
